The kernel learners and the width-2048 network order the levels by input strength alone and ignore the targets; the two-layer linear network orders them by the product c·g in every cell of the first grid; the small-scale ReLU network keeps that direction but compresses its spread, so many cells become simultaneous. Local transfer entropy was near zero at the pinned walls and marked under 3% of sites. While the input was on, the same interchange failed (IIA 0.03 to 0.32): the input put the wall back. A closed pair of walls did not shrink unless shorter than the training minimum; a wall forced by opposite boundary inputs, erased by writing a uniform state, reappeared at the clamped end in four of six networks and not at all in two. | [CASE-371](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-371.md) | Toy transformer forgetting study | A toy-scale stand-in for [CASE-274](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-274.md)'s design, for [LEAD-043](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-043.md). numpy only, CPU, about two hours of compute on a shared machine. | [CASE-384](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-384.md) | Planner, value learner and demons in mazes | [CASE-187](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-187.md) run at toy scale for [LEAD-160](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-160.md). Twenty 8x8 mazes with loops, deterministic and fully observed; goal family "reach cell g" for all 64 cells. A planner (M) holds a learned transition table and plans by value iteration; a policy (P) is goal-conditioned Q-learning with hindsight relabelling; a distributed predictor (D) is one TD-learned demon per (state, action, goal) predicting discounted visits under random continuation, acting by ascent. All three learn from the same random walk and treat unknown moves as "stay", which matches their goal success exactly at every level (0.52, 0.83, 1.0, full coverage); M and P choose identical actions, D 93 to 98% the same on average. Queries answered by reading a transition table out of each agent are equally accurate for all three at every level; within each agent's per-decision computation, M answers next states and distances, P distances, D occupancies. A two-entry edit blocking a passage repairs all of M's failed routes, P's 9% and D's 14%; the same block propagated through every demon by the Woodbury identity repairs all of D's, without a table. After a change or damage M recovers fastest and its prediction error flags exactly the damaged units, where P's and D's TD errors flag 56 to 87% of undamaged ones too; 10% damage first costs M more (success 0.27 against 0.35). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [CASE-385](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-385.md) | Permutation-aligned MLPs and loss barriers | [LEAD-157](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-157.md)'s design run at toy scale on CPU. Two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs are trained in numpy on a task with two redundant cues, A and B. A test that uses no barrier says which cue each net relies on: its accuracy when only A, or only B, carries the label. Pairs are aligned four ways (none, weight matching, activation matching, and rescaling quotiented before weight matching), and at width 5 by an exhaustive search over permutations plus optimised rescaling. The barrier is then measured on the straight line, a trained Bezier curve and a trained one-bend polychain. The aligned linear barrier falls with width for every kind of pair. At width 5, three of four pairs that both rely on cue A keep a loss barrier of 0.09 to 0.25 after the exhaustive search, about as much as pairs relying on different cues (0.15 to 0.54). At widths 64 and 256 an A-net and a B-net are connected after activation matching (0.000). A copy of a net, permuted and rescaled per unit, computes exactly the same function, yet permutation alignment alone leaves it a barrier of 0.19 to 0.59. In a load-by-temperature grid, one cell is flat and poorly connected without alignment. There, alignment plus a trained curve removes the barrier, while the aligned straight line keeps 0.07 error, and the cell's accuracy deficit stays. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

A post-hoc sweep shows the verdict turning on the tolerance. City in country is fairly linear in GPT-2 small (held-out R² 0.82); the other relations less so.
